name: MonarchAiPromptToolbar
title: AiPromptToolbar
wrapsNative: MonarchFlowLayout of standard Button and Toggle, with buttonStyle(.monarch(.ghost, size: .sm)) and a compact ToggleStyle applied to the content
summary: The row of controls under an assistant prompt (web search, templates, mode, model, tone) that gives standard buttons and toggles one compact, quiet style and wraps when they do not fit.
whenToUse: Under a prompt field, for a few options that change how the next message is answered.
whenNotToUse: For text formatting use a formatting toolbar. For actions on a finished answer use the message actions. To choose one of several modes put MonarchAiModeSwitcher in the toolbar rather than several toggles.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the built-in name of the group, "Prompt options".

options.name: content
options.description: The controls in order: standard Buttons, Toggles and pickers. Buttons get the small ghost Monarch button style and Toggles a compact toggle-button style, unless you apply your own.

states.name: toggle on
states.description: Assistant subtle fill, assistant border and assistant strong text; a check mark is added when the person asks for differentiation without colour.

states.name: toggle off
states.description: A ghost button in muted text with no border.

states.name: pressed
states.description: Off: the emphasis background. On: the assistant subtle hover fill.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With the standard disabled(_:) modifier the controls use the disabled text role; a toggle that is on keeps a muted fill and border.

states.name: wrapped
states.description: Controls that do not fit move to a new line.

appearance: Buttons are the small ghost Monarch button. Toggles are transparent with muted text when off and take the assistant (ai) subtle fill, border and strong text when on. The high-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colours.
platformNotes: The web ships AiPromptToolbarButton and AiPromptToolbarToggle; on iOS the standard Button and Toggle are styled by the toolbar, and icon-only controls use .labelStyle(.iconOnly) instead of hideLabel. The web's uncontrolled defaultPressed is not offered: a Toggle takes a binding. Android uses the same names.
accessibility: The toolbar is a container named by label ("Prompt options"); controls are read in order.
A toggle keeps the system Toggle as its accessibility representation, so VoiceOver reads it as a switch with its on or off value; its label does not change with its state.
An icon-only control keeps its title as its spoken name.
Every control is at least 44 by 44 points.
A toggle that is on also differs by its border, and by a check mark when Differentiate Without Colour is on.
Press and state changes are not animated when Reduce Motion is on.
edgeCases: Controls wider than the row get a line of their own and their text wraps.
A control with its own buttonStyle or toggleStyle keeps it.
An empty toolbar takes no height.
